candidate.perspective: UK renewable generation, low-carbon infrastructure and project-finance developers potentially eligible for future public capital allocation.
candidate.structural_condition: The announced Energy Wealth Fund could channel North Sea fiscal revenues to low-carbon infrastructure, but operational rules, budget appropriation and deployed capital are not yet evidenced.
candidate.delta: The UK government announced on 21 October 2026 an Energy Wealth Fund with an initial stated £2 billion contribution and an intended link to future North Sea oil-and-gas revenues.
candidate.mechanism: If appropriated and deployed under accessible rules, earmarked public capital could lower financing barriers or share early-stage project risk; announcements alone do not demonstrate expenditure, additionality or lower electricity bills.
catalysts: 28 October Budget legal appropriations and governance rules
Published eligibility and procurement or financing terms
Signed projects, disbursements, commissioning and independently measured outcomes
candidate.invalidation: No appropriation or legal framework, delayed disbursement, diversion of existing spending rather than additional capital, or lack of viable eligible projects.

evidence.name: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero and HM Treasury, Jackdaw and Energy Wealth Fund announcement

candidate.notes: The £2 billion figure is an announced initial funding intention, not a verified capital transfer or commissioned asset.
